title: "Warmup Schedule"
---

bgms uses a multi-stage warmup schedule to tune MCMC sampler
parameters before collecting posterior samples. The schedule is
defined in `src/mcmc/execution/warmup_schedule.h` and adapts its
structure based on whether edge selection is active.

## Five stages

The warmup period is divided into five stages. Stages 3b and 3c
only apply when edge selection is enabled.

| Stage | Name | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| 1 | Initial exploration | Find a reasonable region of parameter space |
| 2 | Adaptation windows | Tune step size (dual averaging) and mass matrix (Welford) |
| 3a | Terminal window | Final mass matrix and step-size adaptation |
| 3b | Proposal SD learning | Tune element-wise Metropolis proposal SDs with edge selection active |
| 3c | Step-size re-adaptation | Re-adapt the NUTS/HMC step size after edge selection changes the geometry |

### Stage 1: Initial exploration

A short burn-in phase (default: the first 75 iterations). The
sampler explores freely; no mass matrix accumulation occurs. Dual
averaging runs to coarsely tune the step size.

### Stage 2: Adaptation windows

The step size and mass matrix are tuned in expanding windows. The
first window has 25 iterations. Each subsequent window doubles in
size (25 → 50 → 100 → ...) until the stage 3a boundary is reached.
At the end of each window:

1. The accumulated variance from `DiagMassMatrixAccumulator` is
   extracted as the new diagonal mass matrix
2. The step-size heuristic runs again with the new mass matrix
3. Both accumulators are reset for the next window

### Stage 3a: Terminal window

The last adaptation window before edge selection activates. After
this stage, the mass matrix is frozen.

### Stage 3b: Proposal SD learning

When edge selection is active, the model needs element-wise Metropolis
proposal standard deviations for the edge indicator updates. During
stage 3b, edge selection is turned on and the proposal SDs are
tuned via Robbins-Monro updates:

$$
\sigma_{k+1} = \sigma_k \cdot \exp\!\bigl(w_k (\log \alpha_k - \log \alpha^*)\bigr)
$$

where $\alpha_k$ is the observed acceptance probability and $\alpha^*$
is the target (default 0.234). The updated SD is clamped to
$[0.001, 2.0]$.

### Stage 3c: Step-size re-adaptation

After edge selection changes the effective posterior geometry (many
edges may be set to zero), the NUTS/HMC step size needs readjustment.
Stage 3c runs dual averaging one more time with the final mass
matrix and active edge selection.

## Budget allocation

When edge selection is active, the total warmup budget is split as:

- **Stages 1–3a**: 85% of total warmup
- **Stage 3b**: 10% (skipped if fewer than 20 iterations)
- **Stage 3c**: ~5%

When edge selection is inactive, stages 3b and 3c are skipped and
the full budget is allocated to stages 1–3a.

## Warning system

The `WarmupSchedule` tracks a `warning_type` field that records
when the warmup budget is insufficient:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | No warning |
| 1 | Warmup too short for the standard schedule |
| 2 | Proportional fallback used (reduced window sizes) |
| 3 | Limited tuning (fewer adaptation windows) |
| 4 | Proposal SD learning skipped (stage 3b dropped) |

The `warmup_check` table returned by `bgm()` reports these warnings
per chain, accessible via `fit$warmup_check` in R.

## Querying the schedule

The `WarmupSchedule` struct exposes predicate methods used by the
chain runner and samplers:

```cpp
bool in_stage1(int i) const;
bool in_stage2(int i) const;
bool in_stage3a(int i) const;
bool in_stage3b(int i) const;
bool in_stage3c(int i) const;
bool sampling(int i) const;          // i >= total_warmup
bool selection_enabled(int i) const; // i >= stage3b_start (or never)
```

These predicates control when the adaptation controller accumulates
samples, when edge selection is turned on, and when the chain
transitions from warmup to sampling.
